clue.text: Today's hang-up

parts.note: this puzzle ran at Christmas, and the thing hung up on that day by the fireplace is a long woollen sock for gifts

explanation.surface: Somebody's neurosis of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang-up' suggests a psychological complex, but here it is literal: something hung up on Christmas Eve for Father Christmas to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: On Christmas Eve children hang up a long sock to be filled with gifts.

clue.text: Rejected part to act or provide entrance for Demon King

indicators.note: the word part is sent back, read from the end

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round
to do is to act
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor turns down a role in a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime the Demon King traditionally pops up through a hatch in the stage floor. 'Rejected' turns PART into TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged hatch in a stage floor lets the pantomime villain appear in a puff of smoke.

clue.text: When Tiny Tim invoked a universal blessing

definitions.text: When Tiny Tim invoked a universal blessing

parts.words: When Tiny Tim invoked a universal blessing
parts.note: in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, Tiny Tim says 'God bless us, every one!' on the feast day

explanation.surface: Recalls the moment in Dickens when a sick boy blessed everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim is the crippled boy in A Christmas Carol; his blessing comes at the Cratchits' dinner on 25 December.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens sets the Cratchit family dinner, and Tiny Tim's blessing, on 25 December.

clue.text: "Bully" boy in a manner of speaking?

definitions.text: "Bully" boy in a manner of speaking?

parts.words: "Bully" boy in a manner of speaking?

explanation.surface: A thug, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' suggests a tormentor; an Irish bull is a self-contradictory remark, traditionally linked to speakers from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Ireland, to whom the 'Irish bull', a comic contradiction, is traditionally attributed.

clue.text: Wood so described, reading revised version

explanation.surface: A bit of carpentry jargon from the updated text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised version' rearranges READING.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber showing the pattern of its fibres is described as such.

clue.text: No little girl's crime

Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A small girl did nothing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'No little girl' as a big Amy; the 's links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already married to another is a criminal offence.

clue.text: One died for this lady's love

definitions.text: One died for this lady's love

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
love is nil, O, in tennis scores

explanation.surface: A man perished for a woman's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to his beloved, the priestess at Sestos.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to reach the priestess of Sestos he loved.

clue.text: Offers 1 ac fillers

definitions.meaning: the things that fill the item at 1 across, the Christmas sock

explanation.surface: A bare cross-reference: proposals for the 1 across fillers.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' points to 1 across, the Christmas sock; gifts fill it.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer is to give formally; gifts are what fill the Christmas sock.

clue.text: A German river in mid- Surrey helps in delivery of 8

the middle of the word Surrey, its central pair of letters, is what is taken

clue.text: A quiet melody or two

an air is a tune

clue.text: Bright ideas with which I spin out food supplies

clue.text: One spoiled in the exodus

parts.note: in the Book of Exodus the departing Israelites took jewels and clothing from the people of the land of the Nile, 'and they spoiled' them

explanation.surface: A pampered child on the journey out.

clue.text: On Naxos her song appears to end in reverse

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: the word end is to be read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round

explanation.surface: An opera singer's number seems to finish backwards on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: Strauss's opera Ariadne auf Naxos is named after the Cretan princess Theseus abandoned there; 'in reverse' turns END round to DNE.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth, the Cretan princess was abandoned by Theseus on the island, as in Strauss's opera title.

clue.text: A brusque burst of firing from this once

explanation.surface: A short sharp volley came from an old gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' rearranges A BRUSQUE; the gun is an early portable matchlock, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: An early portable gun, used before the musket took over, now obsolete.

clue.text: No OT costume where we live

clue.text: Investment's yield? 504, I would conclude
